items.title: Lights-out Luka Dončić and contagious chemistry: are these Lakers for real?
items.summary:
It’s early days, but after a dramatic roster overhaul and an offseason of team-bonding Dončić is playing at an MVP level and LA are looking like contenders

One of the components of Luka Dončić’s shock trade from the Dallas Mavericks to the Los Angeles Lakers that caused great consternation was that he was just entering his prime as an NBA superstar. The worry was that the move could end that prime before it really even began – unceremoniously uprooting the Slovenian wunderkind from a team custom built around his strengths, fresh off a run to the NBA finals, to one who didn’t really make sense at all. Sure, the bright lights of Hollywood would elevate Dončić’s profile and usher him into a new echelon of stardom. But with Oklahoma City starting their run of dominance and rising stars around the league waiting in the wings, some believed his hopes of title contention (or even a long-elusive MVP award) had vanished.

But the start to this season raises the question: what if they were wrong? Dončić is neck-and-neck with Victor Wembanyama in the MVP race, and the Lakers have the best record in the NBA at 15-3, with the Spurs and 76ers just behind at 15-4. San Antonio and their gargantuan French superstar were title and MVP favorites by a wide margin entering this season. But Dončić and the Lakers are keeping pace by pretty much every margin. Friday night’s NBA Cup showdown will be…
items.t: Lights-out Luka Dončić and contagious chemistry: are these Lakers for real?

items.title: Liam Delap’s struggles are symbolic of damaging Chelsea churn
items.summary:
The constant turnover of players and staff has made consistency an elusive quality at Stamford Bridge

Liam Delap came and went. He joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025 and was hailed by Enzo Maresca as the next Harry Kane. Fast forward a year, though, and there was no chance of Delap joining Kane in England’s World Cup squad. The striker’s form was miserable and the only surprise was that Chelsea made a profit when they sold him to Nottingham Forest for £50m last summer.

On one level it looks like good business. Delap’s only season at Stamford Bridge featured one serious hamstring injury, one league goal, one ridiculous red card and not much else. Analysts at other clubs rated him at Ipswich and felt Chelsea was the wrong fit for his direct style of play. The mistake was less the decision not to give Delap another season, no matter the worries over cover for João Pedro, more the call to sign him in the first place.

Continue reading...
items.t: Liam Delap’s struggles are symbolic of damaging Chelsea churn

items.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend

After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. The Chelsea centre-back pairing were described as playing like “two novices” by Jamie Carragher after they were outfought by Dominic Calvert-Lewin last week. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything,” Carragher concluded. “I’m an angel and a demon,” Éric Cantona says intently during a gripping new documentary about his life on and off the football pitch. “And an angel or a demon, you love him or you hate him. I’m far from being the person with the greatest integrity. I’m far from being the person who always tells the truth. I’m far from being the person who has never been hypocritical. Maybe I’m a good person, but I can also be a flower of evil. It’s the first time in my life I’ve realised this. I am a flower of evil, and I find it very beautiful.”

It’s hard to know what to expect from the only written interview pinned to the release of Cantona: Flower of Evil. Joel Cantona has warned that his famous brother will walk out at any mention of the enduring crisis surrounding Manchester United, whether it’s a question about Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival or the Glazer family’s ruinous ownership of the club.

items.title: Neville, Carragher and the inescapable podcasting feedback loop of doom | Jonathan Liew

Even the best managers can struggle to escape ex-players’ need to manufacture a crisis for content. Enter Michael Carrick …

A podcast studio in Manchester. A production runner pours water into jugs. Gary Neville enters the room with Michael Carrick.

Neville: Just so you know, we’re already filming. This is the intro bit, where we show everyone coming on to set and doing some light banter. It humanises us. The viewer sees it and thinks we’re just mates chatting about football, rather than scions of a global podcast empire commercially obliged to produce an endless scroll of provocative content for money. I always say: why can’t you be both?

items.title: Human flamethrower Aaron Rodgers lays bare the cultural rot at the once-great Steelers
items.summary:
The quarterback’s spectacularly messy exit from Pittsburgh could herald an overdue collapse at one of the NFL’s most famous franchises

Nobody in the world, except maybe Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II, is surprised that the franchise’s marriage of convenience with Aaron Rodgers ended in spectacular flames. Despite their own elevated idea of themselves, Pittsburgh have been one of the NFL’s messiest soap operas for a solid decade. When they linked up with the league’s messiest quarterback, it seemed certain we would get … even more mess. When they doubled down last offseason by hiring the coach with whom Rodgers had fallen out in Green Bay in the late 2010s, the mess became inevitable. We’d seen hints of the approaching drama in the season’s first 11 weeks.

“What the fuck … call it!” Rodgers yelled at McCarthy as he looked for a play in early October.

items.title: ‘Just taking part was a victory’: veterans’ sport helps recovery in Ukraine
items.summary:
Photographer David Levene meets service personnel and veterans at selection trials in Lviv for next year’s Invictus Games in Birmingham

It took a little longer than expected for the 100 or so archers to begin competing inside the large Soviet-era velodrome arena at MoD SKA in Lviv (built for the 1980 Moscow Olympics, it is Ukraine’s only indoor cycling track) on the first day of trials for the team that Ukraine will send to next year’s Invictus Games in Birmingham. The delay gave competitors a little extra time to stretch and practise. Coaches paraded up and down the line, giving some last-minute advice on strategy and technique to the waiting men and women facing down their targets.

Pavlo and Vadym share a laugh during the laser tag trials. Pavlo lost his left leg from a landmine in 2023 and swimming became his path to physical and mental recovery. Vadym suffered a frontline injury in 2022. He set a Ukrainian record for runners with below-knee amputations, completing the 42km Marine Corps Marathon in 3hrs 30m in October 2026.
